minutes.headline: Select Board granted Conrad's Drive-In its license on condition back taxes are resolved by May 20th.
minutes.summary: The board heard a license hearing for a business with unpaid taxes, then met jointly with the School and Finance Committees and the legislative delegation about state aid, Chapter 70, out-of-district costs and busing. Later business included a T-ball request to use the old primary school lot (deferred to March for liability review), a split vote adding two historical commission members, and a member announcing he will not seek reelection.

public_comment.topic: Objected to a cemetery commission donation and rustic wall proposal, alleged conflict of interest over a bench foundation, and asked again for an executive session.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, 282 Pleasant Street, speaking for himself
public_comment.topic: Thanked Mr Franco and objected to the reported request that the delegation meet only with the select board, asking it be discussed publicly.
A finance committee member noted the committee meets Thursday for departmental budget reviews and asked whether the historical commission is set by bylaw rather than charter.

votes.motion: Approve Conrad's Drive-In license at 835 Mass Ave, contingent on back taxes being resolved or a plan in place by May 20th.
School committee adjourn its joint meeting.
Finance committee adjourn its joint meeting (roll call).
Change Kim Duffy from associate to full member of the Green Communities Committee, term to June 30, 2024.
Appoint Anna Lockwood and Heather Shoka to the Historical Commission, term to June 30, 2025.
Commit fiscal year 24 third quarter water commitment.
Approve and sign the warrant for the presidential primaries on March 5th.

budget_items.what_was_said: The senator said the governor clawed back FY24 money because revenue is under projections, with Esser funds ending.
A school committee member said Chapter 70 grows about 1.2% a year, a small per-student hold harmless increase that should be indexed.
A representative cited increases in Chapter 70 and the cherry sheet since taking office.
The school committee chair said the district is near the bottom statewide in per-pupil spending.
The district lost smart growth aid for a year and may see it return; it missed qualifying narrowly.
A representative said Lunenburg got extra Chapter 90 funds from fair share this year.
A representative described a one-time reserve for rural and suburban districts facing out-of-district cost increases.
A board member said one child's services take many households' taxes.
A school committee member said busing is a notable part of the school budget with only one bidder.
A 48-month contract was signed starting November 2024 at a rate below the current aggregation rate.
The board committed the FY24 third quarter water bills.
An accounts payable warrant was presented for signature.
Real estate technical assistance funds must be spent by June 30th.
The water district listed an entry-level position with an hourly wage.

decisions.decision: T-ball request to use the old primary school lot will return to an agenda in early March after the town manager works out liability and insurance terms; any agreement to be year-to-year.
Chair clarified there is no select board prohibition on the delegation meeting other boards; he prefers one joint legislative-priorities meeting.
Warrant for annual town meeting open until March 18th.
Upcoming meetings set for March 5, 12 and 19; caucus March 25.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved Conrad's Drive-In license on condition that back taxes are resolved or a payment plan is in place by May 20th.
The board met jointly with the School and Finance Committees and the legislative delegation on state aid, Chapter 70, out-of-district costs and busing.
The senator said the governor clawed back FY24 money because state revenue is under projections.
The board deferred a Little League T-ball request to use the old primary school lot to an early March agenda, pending liability and insurance terms.
The board appointed two Historical Commission members on a 3-2 vote and signed the warrant for the March 5th presidential primaries 5-0.

why_it_matters: State aid, Chapter 70 and out-of-district costs shape how much of the school budget falls on the local tax levy, and the joint meeting put those pressures before the delegation.
A mid-year state cut and a business with unpaid taxes both bear on the town's revenue picture, and the May 20th condition sets a date for the second.
watch_next: May 20th, the deadline for Conrad's Drive-In to resolve its back taxes or have a payment plan in place.
Early March, when the T-ball request returns to the agenda; the warrant for annual town meeting stays open until March 18th.
